title: The Kingdom of Majorca's lands on the mainland (Perpinyà, Prades, Puigcerdà and Montpellier) pass to Aragon; with the Balearics gone to Morocco, the kingdom is no more
The Sultan of the Mamluks agrees to betroth his daughter Aiman to Saʿd, heir of Granada: the alliance with Cairo is now a bond of blood
The Chancellor reports that the heir Saʿd, not yet three, is a Prodigy, and the court begins to whisper that he may be the ruler to lead the Emirate out of the darkness
source: Trent's screenshot of the event and his account (January 1351)

title: The finest tutors of the Islamic world, and several Christians among them, are summoned to Gharnāṭa to begin the extensive education of the heir Saʿd

With Castile at a tipping point, Gharnāṭa makes a quiet offer: it will not fund the Moroccans, in exchange for a mild shift of the border along the river toward Ishbīliyya, giving it Qarmūna and, north of it, the silver mines of Qusanṭīna
source: Trent's account (January 1351, day approximate); tax figures from the save of 1350-09-02

title: Castile pays for Granada's silence: Qarmūna and the silver mines of Qusanṭīna are ceded to Gharnāṭa, moving the border down the river toward Ishbīliyya. Granada now holds 55 of the 72 locations of the Strait

Morocco surrenders to Castile, ending the Second Moroccan War. By the peace's terms Morocco gives up its treaties with Granada: Castile has done Granada's dirty work, and the alliance with the Marīnids is ended without Granada breaking it
After the war: sovereignty 61.2 and Morocco's influence over Granada 11.1; stability 13.9, the treasury 912 and no debt; the Mamlūks the only ally

The amir sets out east to make the Hajj, half a year ahead of the pilgrimage season in Dhū al-Ḥijja (about 2 February 1352), for the road is long. His elder brother Faraj ibn Ismāʿīl governs as regent in his absence; the caravan is stocked and guarded, and it bears the maḥmal in all manner of splendour
source: Trent's account. The game names a Naṣr al-Stijjai as regent; the chronicle makes Faraj the regent at Trent's direction

title: A House of Learning: while the amir is on the Hajj, the regent Faraj founds the Great Madrasa of Gharnāṭa beside the great mosque, where the law will be taught under one roof as in the cities of the East, to draw students and jurists from across the Strait and bind the learning of the cities to the service of the amir

data.choice: Found the Great Madrasa beside the great mosque.
data.historical: Yūsuf I founded the Madrasa Yūsufiyya beside the great mosque in 1349

source: Trent's screenshot of the event, with the chosen option's tooltip open

title: Another traitor: Najīb al-ʿĀbidīn of the ʿulamāʾ, handed over to Qashtāla at its demand as Granada's overlord, takes baptism before the cathedral chapter as Ramiro, a Castilian, carrying the letters, treatises and reckoning tables of the libraries of Qurṭuba with him, five days after the Great Madrasa was founded

data.castileChoice: A useful soul gained for the faith.

source: Trent's screenshots of Castile's event and its breakdown; Trent calls him a traitor

title: The Royal Hajj reaches al-Qāhira, the City of a Thousand Minarets, under the shadow of al-Azhar. The amir has the caravan adorned in banners and silk and waits ten days in the city, so that Cairo may see the splendour of the Emirate

data.event: The Royal Ḥajj: The City of a Thousand Minarets
data.choice: Adorn the caravan in banners and silk, then wait.

source: Trent's screenshot of the event, with the chosen option's tooltip open
